address: Treaty Road and Spring Street, Woodstock, Cape Town
propertyDescription: A historic white milkwood tree associated with the signing of the treaty following the Battle of Blaauwberg.
locationClue: Find the historic milkwood tree in Woodstock associated with the beginning of the second British occupation of the Cape.

questions.question: What historical event is associated with the Treaty Tree?
options: The transfer of the Cape following the Battle of Blaauwberg
questions.explanation: The treaty signed on 10 January 1806 marked the transfer of the Cape to British control.

questions.question: On what date was the treaty signed?
questions.explanation: The treaty was signed on 10 January 1806.

questions.question: Which tree species is the Treaty Tree?
questions.explanation: The Treaty Tree is a white milkwood tree.

commemorates: The history of the Baptist Church of Troyeville
propertyDescription: A historic Johannesburg church founded in 1897. The present church building was begun in 1909.
locationClue: Find the historic Baptist church in the Johannesburg suburb of Troyeville.

questions.question: In which year was the Baptist Church of Troyeville founded?
questions.explanation: The congregation was founded in 1897 in a small wood and iron building.

questions.question: What was the original building known as?
questions.explanation: The original wood and iron structure was known as the Tin Tabernacle.

questions.question: When did construction of the present church building begin?
questions.explanation: The present building was begun in 1909, with its spire erected in 1911.
